transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Time: 3:00 PM PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Rachel Gomez (CISO, SummitCare), Mark Patel (Head of ML), Theo Park (Infra Lead)

Summary: (auto) security & privacy review focused on data retention, encryption, PII/PHI, audit logging, and contractual assurances about model training.
Topics: SOC 2 / ISO, RBAC / SSO, audit logs, encryption / KMS, data residency, prompt retention, PII/PHI, training-on-customer-data

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:05] Rachel: hi, rachel here, summitcare ciso. we've got mark on the line for the ml requirements, theo for infra. thanks for fitting this in.
[00:12] Ava: of course, i'll hand to liam for the technical overview then we'll go into questions.
[00:17] Liam: hi team, liam, se at redwood. we'll cover architecture, data flows, encryption, and retention. feel free to interrupt.
[00:25] Mark: quick framing from our side — we're evaluating for patient-facing summarization workflows, so PHI is definitely in scope. primary concerns are: no model training on our data, strict retention policy, keys under our control if possible, and auditability.
[00:40] Liam: understood. starting high level: hosted api (redwood hosted) vs dedicated vs private. hosted gives fastest onboarding but default configs retain prompts/outputs short-term for debugging and customer support unless configured otherwise; dedicated/reserved keeps isolation; private (vpc / on-prem) gives the most control — e.g., customer-managed KMS and network isolation.
[01:05] Theo: when you say "retain" — what's the default window for hosted? and is there an option to opt out of retention entirely?
[01:12] Ava: default is 30 days for debug logs in hosted, but there are toggles. to be clear, we do not use customer prompts or outputs to train our models for hosted customers by default — there's contractual language for that. i'll let liam expand on the no-training guarantee.
[01:25] Liam: right, we have two layers: a product/config layer and a legal/contract layer. product-wise, no training pipelines consume customer data unless explicitly enabled. we do have telemetry/ops logs but those are scrubbed; training datasets are separate. contractually we can put explicit "no training on customer data" clauses in the msa and dpa.
[01:44] Rachel: okay, can you give specifics on where that clause sits? we need it in the dpa and also an appendix around PHI.
[01:50] Ava: yes, we can include that in the DPA and MSA — standard redwood enterprise addendum. i'll attach a sample clause.
[01:55] Mark: on encryption: do you support customer-managed keys? bring your own KMS?
[01:59] Liam: yes for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) — keys never leave your control. for hosted we offer server-side encryption with our KMS; there is a managed-KMS option where we rotate keys, but for regulated patients we'd recommend Private with BYOK.
[02:21] Theo: and audit logs — what granularity do you provide? we need per-request logs with token/response hashing rather than full content dumps.
[02:28] Liam: we emit structured audit logs per request: timestamp, route, model, token counts, requester id, and hashed content pointer (we can ship content-less pointers). full transcripts are only stored if retention is enabled. logs can be routed to customer's log sink (S3, GCS, Splunk) for long-term retention.
[02:45] Rachel: is there an out-of-the-box RBAC and SSO? we need SSO with SAML/SCIM and role-based controls for who can access logs and keys.
[02:54] Liam: yes, console supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, and RBAC roles. by default you can restrict audit-log access to admin roles. for Private we can integrate with your IdP directly so keys and console are behind your SSO.
[03:10] Mark: you mentioned training pipelines are separate — is there any scenario where aggregated customer data could leak into model training?
[03:18] Liam: not in normal operations. we have strict separation: training data is versioned and curated by our applied ml team; it's not automatically fed from customer buckets. there was a minor misconfiguration historically at an industry peer, but redwood's infra has guardrails and an approval workflow before any dataset ingestion for training.
[03:36] Rachel: regarding retention for prompts — can we set retention to zero for hosted? or do we need private to avoid any transient storage?
[03:44] Ava: product currently allows minimizing retention — short-term ephemeral for processing. however if legal requires zero retention we recommend Private deployment where logs can be entirely within your VPC and retention policy enforced by your infra.
[03:58] Theo: curious about in-transit and at-rest encryption — you said you support TLS and KMS at rest, any FIPS modules or HSM integrations?
[04:07] Liam: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit. at rest we integrate with cloud KMS; for HSM-level we support HSM-backed KMS for Private. FIPS 140-2 validated modules are available via customer KMS providers.
[04:22] Mark: auditability — how long are logs kept by default and can we configure export?
[04:27] Liam: default audit retention in hosted is 90 days for analytics logs, 30 days for request transcripts. but we strongly recommend exporting logs to your archive — we support continuous export to S3/GCS.
[04:40] Rachel: we need per-tenant segregation — would dedicated be enough or must we go private?
[04:46] Liam: dedicated reserves GPU capacity and tenancy isolation but control plane is still redwood-managed; for full tenancy + network isolation + BYOK choose Private. many regulated customers pick Private.
[04:57] Rachel: ok. another thing—PII/PHI discovery and redaction — do you provide any tooling or SDKs?
[05:03] Liam: we provide client-side SDKs with optional pre-send redaction hooks; additionally we have NAIVE built-in pattern matching and a partner ecosystem for automated redaction. but for high-assurance PHI redaction customers often run in-proc redaction on prem.
[05:18] Mark: can we get a whitepaper or runbook on how to integrate redwood with our DLP?
[05:22] Ava: yes, we'll share an integration runbook and best practices.
[05:25] Theo: about the 'no training' guarantee — is it auditable? can you provide attestation?
[05:30] Liam: we can provide contractual attestation and include it in the DPA. on the technical side, we can show separation of storage buckets/paths and provide a data flow diagram. we also have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence for controls.
[05:44] Rachel: will you share SOC 2 and ISO artifacts?
[05:47] Ava: yes, i'll send SOC 2 Type II report and the ISO27001 cert — redacted where necessary — after an NDA if required.
[05:54] Rachel: ok. compliance question: data residency — can you guarantee data stays in region X (us-east-1) for a hosted solution?
[06:01] Liam: we can route requests regionally; however hosted multi-region availability may route within the region. for contractual guarantees we typically recommend dedicated or Private pinned to specific region.
[06:14] Mark: what about redaction in logs — you said hashed pointers. how reversible are those? we want to avoid reversible hashes in your systems.
[06:23] Liam: we use one-way hashing with salted keys; for extra assurance we can omit content entirely and only store metadata pointers that you control.
[06:33] Rachel: are there any background telemetry or analytics features that capture usage patterns that could contain PII?
[06:40] Liam: telemetry is aggregated; we scrub PII from usage metrics. raw transcripts are only available if retention is enabled; otherwise we keep only aggregated metrics.
[06:49] Ava: happy to add a contractual addendum that enumerates what telemetry is captured and what is scrubbed.
[06:55] Mark: ok, on legal — we will want 'no training' language, data residency clause, and details on breach notification timing.
[07:02] Rachel: what is your standard breach notification SLA?
[07:06] Ava: standard is 72 hours for incidents that materially affect customer data; we can discuss a tighter SLA in enterprise contracts.
[07:15] Theo: for the private deployment, what's the expected timeline to stand up? we have dedicated infra windows.
[07:20] Liam: typical private deployment with our helm chart and infra automation takes 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS provisioning; pilot can begin earlier with a limited feature set.
[07:33] Mark: liability and data processing — do you accept customer-required subprocessor lists?
[07:38] Ava: yes, we list subprocessors and accept reasonable contractual controls; we also support subprocessors disclosure and on-request audits.
[07:46] Rachel: one more — deletion: if we ask for deletion of all customer data, what's the process and verification?
[07:53] Liam: we have a deletion workflow: deprovision access, remove snapshots, zero out storage, and provide a deletion certificate. for Private, the process is executed in-customer infra and you can verify logs locally.
[08:08] Mark: let's talk about data used for model evals — do you allow customers to opt in to let you use anonymized data for evaluations?
[08:15] Liam: only with explicit opt-in; opt-in surfaces in the admin console and must be affirmed contractually. and we maintain separate datasets for evals, with provenance markers.
[08:27] Rachel: great. any known gaps in the redwood offering for healthcare PHI?
[08:33] Liam: main gap for some customers is that hosted defaults may not meet strict zero-retention/regionality requirements — that's why Private is recommended. we also recommend customer-side redaction before sending anything sensitive.
[08:45] Ava: quick note — we also have a HIPAA BAA option for enterprise customers; we can share the BAA template.
[08:52] Rachel: please do.
[08:54] Theo: are there sample configs for KMS rotation and key policies?
[08:58] Liam: yes — i'll attach key policy examples and rotation schedules.
[09:03] Mark: how about pen tests and vulnerability management — do you publish schedules?
[09:08] Ava: we do annual third-party pentests and publish summary reports; for enterprise customers we can share remediation timelines under NDA.
[09:18] Rachel: okay wrapping up — principal concerns are: contractual "no training" language, private deployment option with BYOK, retention set to zero or within your control, and robust audit/export to our log sink.
[09:31] Ava: noted. next steps — we'll send SOC 2/ISO docs, KMS integration docs, BAA template, and architecture diagram. set a follow-up tech deep-dive to scope Private pilot.
[09:42] Mark: thanks, that works.
[09:45] Rachel: thanks all.

Action items (verbatim in transcript):
- Ava to share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 cert (may require NDA)
- Liam to share KMS integration runbook and architecture diagram
- Ava to share BAA template and DPA sample with no-training clause
- Schedule deeper on-site tech session with infra team

End of call.
